rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ in innahu is the pronoun of the matter: the matter is as follows.
rows.anchor: ضمير الشأن يعني أن الأمر والشأن كذا وكذا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila infer a definitive threat for major sinners: every major sinner is a criminal, and the conditional man is general because any individual may be excepted.
rows.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية في القطع على وعيد أصحاب الكبائر

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين من أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of al-Rāzī’s fellow theologians deny that a major sinner is called a criminal, since the passage contrasts the criminal with the believer; they also cite 83:29.
rows.anchor: واعترض بعض المتكلمين من أصحابنا على هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين من أصحابنا
rows.claim: The objectors add that a major sinner, even if punished in the Fire, does not remain in the condition of neither dying nor living described here.
rows.anchor: والمؤمن صاحب الكبيرة وإن عذب بالنار لا يكون بهذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection cites a report graded sound: whoever has a particle’s weight of faith in his heart will leave the Fire.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر الصحيح : ( يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من الإيمان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with believers only answers the Muʿtazila if major sinners are believers, which their own doctrine denies; the objection assumes its proponents’ position.
rows.anchor: هذا إنما ينفع لو ثبت أن صاحب الكبيرة مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description does not exclude a major sinner, because Hell’s punishment is extremely severe; al-Rāzī cites 3:192.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم فإن عذاب جهنم في غاية الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed answer is that the Qurʾān is mass-transmitted and cannot be opposed by a solitary report.
rows.anchor: القرآن متواتر فلا يعارضه خبر الواحد

rows.speaker: الخصم
rows.claim: A counterargument allows a solitary report to specify the Qurʾān in practical rulings, but says its probabilistic force cannot settle a matter of belief.
rows.anchor: يجوز تخصيص القرآن بخبر الواحد وللخصم أن يجيب فيقول ذلك يفيد الظن

rows.speaker: معترض آخر
rows.claim: Another objector says the threat is agreed to be conditional on absence of repentance and of reward that cancels punishment; those without divine pardon must enter Hell.
rows.anchor: فإن اعترض إنسان آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No separate repentance condition is needed: the verse describes someone arriving before God as a criminal, which does not describe a repentant person.
rows.anchor: أما شرط نفي التوبة فلا حاجة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A minor sinner is not called a criminal, since mujrim is a term of blame and should not be applied to someone who commits a minor sin.
rows.anchor: وأما صاحب الصغيرة فلأنه لا يسمى مجرما لأن المجرم اسم للذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound objection is that the general threat conflicts with the following general promise for a believer who did righteous deeds and later committed a major sin.
rows.anchor: الاعتراض الصحيح أن نقول : عموم هذا الوعيد معارض بما جاء بعده من عموم الوعد

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila say the sin’s punishment cancels the reward of prior obedience, so the promise does not rescue the major sinner.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : عقاب المعصية يحبط ثواب الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī counters that the reward of faith may instead repel the punishment for sin.
rows.anchor: قلنا : لم لا يجوز أن يقال : ثواب الإيمان يدفع عقاب المعصية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila object that if faith’s reward offset sin, the major sinner should neither be cursed nor subjected to a legal penalty.
rows.anchor: لو كان كذلك لوجب أن لا يجوز لعنه وإقامة الحد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says cursing such a person is impermissible, while a legal penalty may serve as a trial, as with a repentant person, or as deterrence.
rows.anchor: وأما إقامة الحد عليه فقد تكون على سبيل المحنة كما في حق التائب

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Citing 5:38, the Muʿtazila argue that a penalty imposed as deterrence precludes deserving praise and honor, and therefore eliminates reward.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة قوله تعالى : { والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the deterrent-penalty text conflicts with texts granting reward, with no basis to privilege either: believers include thieves and non-thieves, and thieves include believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: النص الدال على إقامة الحد عليه على سبيل التنكيل صار معارضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generality of man is only probabilistic, whereas this doctrinal issue requires certainty; al-Rāzī refers readers to al-Maḥṣūl for the full argument.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم أن كلمة من في إفادة العموم قطعية بل ظنية ومسألتنا قطعية

rows.speaker: المجسمة
rows.claim: The corporealists argue that a body could come to its Lord only if the Lord occupied a place.
rows.anchor: تمسكت المجسمة بقوله : { إنه من يأت ربه مجرما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that coming to God means metaphorically coming to the place of the promised reward, as Abraham said he was going to his Lord (37:99).
rows.anchor: جعل إتيانهم موضع الوعد إتيانا إلى الله مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a living body must be either alive or dead, the verse means the person suffers Hell’s worst state: no relieving death and no enjoyable life.
rows.anchor: فمعناه في الآية أنه يكون في جهنم بأسوء حال لا يموت موتة مريحة ولا يحيا حياة ممتعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording could imply that the believer performed every righteous deed, that is neither agreed to be required nor possible; it means fulfillment of obligations.
rows.anchor: يقتضي أن يكون آتيا بكل الصالحات

words: جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest ranks promised to believers are explained as Gardens of Eden with rivers flowing beneath them.
rows.anchor: فسرها فقال : { جنات عدن تجرى من تحتها الانهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the highest ranks are assigned to believers who come with faith and righteous deeds, lesser ranks must belong to others, namely sinful believers whom God pardons.
rows.anchor: فسائر الدرجات التي هي غير عالية لا بد وأن تكون لغيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses purification here as saying, There is no god but God.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : يريد من قال لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī reasons that lesser ranks are not the reward of the purified, so they belong to sinners from the faithful whom God pardons by grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: لما دلت هذه الآية على أن الدرجات العالية هي جزاء من تزكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān itself does not state that Pharaoh carried out his threat against the believing people, though reports establish that he did.
rows.anchor: ليس في القرآن أن فرعون فعل بأولئك القوم المؤمنين ما أوعدهم به ولكن ثبت ذلك في الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika connects to the earlier kadhālika naquṣṣu: in the same way and manner, God continually sent down the whole Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: قوله : { وكذالك } عطف على قوله : { كذالك نقص } أي ومثل ذلك لا نزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is Arabic so Arabs can understand it, recognize its inimitability and composition, and see that it is unlike human speech.
rows.anchor: كونه عربيا لتفهمه العرب فيقفوا على إعجازه ونظمه وخروجه عن جنس كلام البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarrafnā min al-waʿīd means that warnings were repeated and elaborated; this includes explaining commands and prohibitions, since repetition of warning entails setting out rulings.
rows.anchor: أي كررناه وفصلناه ويدخل تحت الوعيد بيان الفرائض والمحارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā here means avoiding prohibited acts and leaving obligations; al-Rāzī links this gloss to 2:183.
rows.anchor: والمراد اتقاء المحرمات وترك الواجبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, the Qurʾān was sent to make people wary of what they should avoid, or to awaken remembrance that prompts obedience and good deeds.
rows.anchor: إنا إنما أنزلنا القرآن لأجل أن يصيروا متقين أي محترزين عما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān can be said to produce remembrance because remembrance arises upon its recitation, so the effect is attributed to its cause.
rows.anchor: لما حصل الذكر عند قراءته أضيف الذكر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā is not attributed to the Qurʾān because it is continued abstention from an original non-action, whereas newly occurring remembrance can be attributed to it.
rows.anchor: وذلك استمرار على العدم الأصلي فلم يجز إسناده إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although or normally signals alternatives and taqwā requires remembrance, the construction resembles saying, Keep company with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn: do not be without either.
rows.anchor: هذا كقولهم جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين أي لا تكن خاليا منهما فكذا ههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading is that the Qurʾān was sent for taqwā; if that does not occur, it will at least bring remembrance, honor, and a good reputation.
rows.anchor: إنا أنزلنا القرآن ليتقوا فإن لم يحصل ذلك فلا أقل من أن يحدث القرآن لهم ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either reading, the Qurʾān’s descent brings taqwā, broadly understood as its intended religious benefit.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذين التقديرين يكون إنزاله تقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After magnifying the Qurʾān, God magnifies Himself; He is called the true King because His sovereignty neither vanishes nor changes, is not received from another, and belongs to no one more rightfully.
rows.anchor: فقال : { فتعالى الله الملك الحق } تنبيها على ما يلزم خلقه من تعظيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿālā is a form of tafāʿala from height; divine height, greatness, and lordship share the sense of attributes of majesty beyond imagination and intellect.
rows.anchor: وتعالى تفاعل من العلو وقد ثبت أن علوه وعظمته وربوبيته بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is transcendent above benefit and harm: He sent the Qurʾān to guide people, not to gain from obedience or suffer from disobedience; obedience occurs by His enabling and sins by His justice, each person being facilitated toward what he was created for.
rows.anchor: وهو منزه عن المنافع والمضار فهو تعالى إنما أنزل القرآن ليحترزوا عما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says the discourse from the question about the mountains (20:105) ends here, and do not hasten with the Qurʾān begins a new address.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : إن من قوله : { ويسئلونك عن الجبال }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported context says the Prophet feared missing part of the revelation and recited along with the angel; he was told to listen until the angel finished, then recite, since God would preserve him from error and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام كان يخاف من أن يفوته منه شيء فيقرأ مع الملك فأمره بأن يسكت حال قراءة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible meaning is that the Prophet should not hurry to recite the Qurʾān inwardly to himself.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد لا تعجل بقراءته في نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible meaning is that he should not hurry to deliver the Qurʾān to someone else.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن لا تعجل في تأديته إلى غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possible meaning is that he should not rush to settle on its apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل في اعتقاد ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth possible meaning is that he should not explain to others what its apparent meaning entails before the revelation is complete.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل في تعريف الغير ما يقتضيه ظاهره

words: مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the revelation is completed can refer either to completion of its text or to clarification of its meaning, both of which require revelation.
rows.anchor: تمامه ، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد من قبل أن يقضى إليك بيانه

words: مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precise rule is to restrain oneself and others until the text or its explanation is complete, since an utterance may still be qualified by an exception, condition, or other specification.
rows.anchor: يجب التوقف في معنى الكلام ما لم يأت عليه الفراغ لما يجوز أن يحصل عقيبه من استثناء أو شرط

rows.speaker: مقاتل والسدي
rows.claim: Muqātil and al-Suddī, with a transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ, say the Prophet rapidly repeated Gabriel’s recitation from fear of forgetting; he was told to wait until it ended, receive it calmly, and trust God to increase his understanding and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مقاتل والسدي ورواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda interpret the command as forbidding recitation to the Companions before the meanings had been revealed and explained.
rows.anchor: فتقرأه على أصحابك قبل أن يوحى إليك بيان معانيه وهذا قول مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that Meccans and the bishop of Najrān demanded answers within three days; delayed revelation fueled a claim that the Jews had defeated Muḥammad, so this reading forbids hastening revelation’s descent through its stages from the Preserved Tablet to him.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : إن أهل مكة وأسقف نجران قالوا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan transmits an account in which a woman said her husband slapped her face; the Prophet ordered retaliation, then withheld it when this verse was revealed until 4:34 came down.
rows.anchor: روى الحسن أن امرأة أتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī calls the account from al-Ḥasan remote and says the detailed explanation given first is the one to rely on.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد والاعتماد على التفصيل الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means that the Prophet should turn to God for increased knowledge, which comes through completion of the Qurʾān or clarification of what was revealed.
rows.anchor: أمره بالفزع إلى الله سبحانه في زيادة العلم التي تظهر بتمام القرآن أو بيان ما نزل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked how hastening could be forbidden if done by revelation, al-Rāzī answers that the Prophet may have acted by personal reasoning, though refraining would have been preferable.
rows.anchor: لعله فعله بالاجتهاد ، وكان الأولى تركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the sixth Qurʾānic telling of Adam’s story, following al-Baqara, al-Aʿrāf, al-Ḥijr, al-Isrāʾ, and al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: المرة السادسة من قصة آدم عليه السلام في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story fulfills the earlier promise to relate reports of the past in 20:99.
rows.anchor: انجازا للوعد في قوله : { كذالك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placed after the Qurʾān’s warnings, Adam’s disobedience shows that humans have long failed to guard against Satan’s whispers: even a direct warning that he was an enemy did not prevent Adam’s lapse.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال : إن طاعة بني آدم للشيطان وتركهم التحفظ من وساوسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the command to seek more knowledge, Adam’s forgetfulness despite repeated warning illustrates human weakness and the need to ask God for knowledge and protection from forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعده قصة آدم عليه السلام فإنه بعدما عهد الله إليه وبالغ في تجديد العهد وتحذيره من العدو نسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s excessive zeal in religious effort is juxtaposed with Adam’s negligence: humans may err through either excess or shortfall.
rows.anchor: فلما وصفه بالإفراط وصف آدم بالتفريط في ذلك فإنه تساهل في ذلك ولم يتحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet may have worried that the prohibition implied wrongdoing; the story reassures him that his haste sprang from devotion and care for revelation, unlike Adam’s lapse through neglect.
rows.anchor: فقيل له : إن كنت فعلت ما نهيت عنه فإنما فعلته حرصا منك على العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant here means a divine command or prohibition, as when a king gives instructions or a charge.
rows.anchor: فلا شك أن المراد بالعهد أمر من الله تعالى أو نهي منه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say Adam was charged not to eat from the tree or even approach it.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : عهدنا إليه أن لا يأكل من الشجرة ولا يقربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of min qablu is before those who received the Qurʾānic warnings.
rows.anchor: أحدها : من قبل هؤلاء الذين صرفنا لهم الوعيد في القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes min qablu to mean before Adam ate from the tree, when God had charged him not to eat from it.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : قال ابن عباس : من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes min qablu to mean before Muḥammad and the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن وهو قول الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes nasiya in its ordinary opposite-of-remembering sense: Adam was reproached for insufficient attention and retention, which led to forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وإنما عوتب على ترك التحفظ والمبالغة في الضبط حتى تولد منه النسيان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan swore that Adam never disobeyed except through forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وكان الحسن رحمه الله يقول : والله ما عصى قط إلا بنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view reads nasiya as left or neglected: Adam abandoned the charge to avoid the tree and ate its fruit.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن المراد بالنسيان الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant, fa-nassāhu al-shayṭān, makes Satan the one who caused Adam to forget; on this reading, the act may have been deliberate without interpretation or committed under an interpretation, as discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : فنسي أي فنساه الشيطان ، وعلى هذا التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajada may mean knew, as in this phrase, or its opposite of nonexistence, yielding the sense that Adam lacked resolve.
rows.anchor: الوجود يجوز أن يكون بمعنى العلم ومنه ولم نجد له عزما وأن يكون نقيض العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm means firm determination and steadfastness.
rows.anchor: العزم هو التصميم والتصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible gloss is that Adam lacked resolve to persist in sin, which makes the phrase closer to praise.
rows.anchor: ولم نجد له عزما على القيام على المعصية فيكون إلى المدح أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he lacked resolve to abandon the sin.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد ولم نجد له عزما على ترك المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that Adam lacked resolve to guard himself against heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أو لم نجد له عزما على التحفظ والاحتراز عن الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Adam’s mistake came through personal reasoning, the phrase may mean that he lacked resolve to exercise due care in how he reasoned.
rows.anchor: إذا قلنا : إنه عليه السلام إنما أخطأ بالاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī lists questions about whether all or some angels were commanded, what prostration means, whether Iblīs was an angel and how he was addressed, Adam’s rank relative to Muḥammad, and how refusal made Iblīs an unbeliever; he refers to al-Baqara for full discussion.
rows.anchor: أن هذه المسائل مرت على سبيل الاستقصاء في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for Iblīs’s enmity is envy of the divine favors Adam received.
rows.anchor: أن إبليس كان حسودا فلما رآى آثار نعم الله تعالى في حق آدم عليه السلام حسده فصار عدوا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation contrasts the young, learned Adam, taught the names (2:31), with the old, ignorant Iblīs, whose claim of superiority by ancestry showed ignorance; an old ignorant person is an enemy to a young scholar.
rows.anchor: أن آدم كان شابا عالما لقوله وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ، وإبليس كان شيخا جاهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation says the enmity persisted because Iblīs was made from fire and Adam from water and earth, so their origins were opposed.
rows.anchor: أن إبليس مخلوق من النار وآدم مخلوق من الماء والتراب فبين أصليهما عداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God is the one who expelled Adam and Eve, it is properly attributed to Satan because his seduction caused the act that led to their expulsion.
rows.anchor: لما كان بوسوسته هو الذي فعل ما ترتب عليه الخروج صح ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam alone is named as suffering because the hardship of a household is included in that of its male head and ruler, while the phrasing also preserves the verse’s cadence.
rows.anchor: أن في ضمن شقاء الرجل وهو قيم أهله وأميرهم شقاءهم كما أن في ضمن سعادته سعادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that the suffering means the labor of seeking food, which falls on the man rather than the woman.
rows.anchor: أريد بالشقاء التعب في طلب القوت وذلك على الرجل دون المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says a red bull was sent down to Adam; he plowed with it and wiped sweat from his brow.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر وكان يحرث عليه ويمسح العرق عن جبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase wa-annaka is read with either fatḥ or kasrah; fatḥ coordinates with an lā tajūʿa. Though an does not normally precede another an, the wāw can stand for any governing particle, not only an.
rows.anchor: قرىء وإنك بالفتح والكسر ووجه الفتح العطف على أن لا تجوع فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satiety, drinking, clothing, and shade are the four pillars of human well-being; God grants them in the Garden without earning or effort.
rows.anchor: الشبع والري والكسوة والإكتنان في الظل هي الأقطاب التي يدور عليها أمر الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings are expressed by negating their opposites so Adam hears forms of hardship and becomes especially wary of the cause that would bring them.
rows.anchor: وذكرها بلفظ النفي لأضدادها التي هي الجوع والعري والظمأ والضحى ليطرق سمعه شيئا من أصناف الشقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freedom from hunger, nakedness, thirst, and sun exposure explains the misery mentioned in the preceding warning.
rows.anchor: تفسير الشقاء المذكور في قوله : { فتشقى }

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim explains the dual descend as addressing Adam with his descendants and Iblīs with his descendants; each is a kind, so the dual fits, while each kind’s multitude explains the following plural you.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : الخطاب لآدم ومعه ذريته ولإبليس ومعه ذريته

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that Adam and Eve are the source from whom humanity descended, so they are treated as humanity itself and addressed in the plural.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : لما كان آدم وحواء عليهما السلام أصلا للبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address and promise of guidance indicate that the descendants of Adam are intended.
rows.anchor: فيه دلالة على أن المراد الذرية

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the wording is satisfied by Satan and devils being enemies to people and people being enemies to them; reciprocal enmity within each side may also be included.
rows.anchor: فقال القاضي : يكفي في توفية هذا الظاهر حقه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the promised guidance as the messengers.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلفوا في المراد بالهدى ، فقال بعضهم : الرسل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others identify the promised guidance as proofs and indications, while another group identifies it as the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم قال : الآخر والأدلة وبعضهم قال القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s synthesis is that guidance means indication broadly and therefore includes messengers, proofs, and the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أن الهدى عبارة عن الدلالة فيدخل فيه كل ذلك

words: فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the promise concerns following evidence, following must include both using the evidence to reason and acting on it; such a follower is promised neither error nor misery.
rows.anchor: واتباعها لا يتكامل إلا بأن يستدل بها وبأن يعمل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that the follower will not go astray in this world or suffer in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لا يضل في الدنيا ولا يشقى في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading places both the absence of error and misery in the afterlife, where God guides the person to the Garden and enables him to dwell there.
rows.anchor: لا يضل ولا يشقى في الآخرة لأنه تعالى يهديه إلى الجنة ويمكنه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading places both promises in this world.
rows.anchor: لا يضل ولا يشقى في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a follower of guidance may face worldly hardship, the promise means no religious error and no suffering caused by religion; hardship from another source is not excluded.
rows.anchor: المراد لا يضل في الدين ولا يشقى بسبب الدين فإن حصل الشقاء بسبب آخر فلا بأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr may refer to the Qurʾān or to the other scriptures God sent.
rows.anchor: والذكر يقع على القرآن وعلى سائر كتب الله تعالى على ما تقدم بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible referent for dhikr is the proofs and indications.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد به الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍank originally means narrowness and hardship; it is a verbal noun that is also used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: فالضنك أصله الضيق والشدة وهو مصدر ثم يوصف به
